title: My signal filter looked useless by hit rate. It was removing the expensive mistakes.
author: Huge_Position890

comments.author: Alphanet_dogwalker
comments.body: how are the 200 signal blocks ordered? With 490 coins, one market move could show up across several blocks. i'd be curious whether the result holds if you shuffle whole time windows with all coins kept together, especially since the 24h returns overlap. The average gap could stay the same while the uncertainty gets a lot bigger

replies.author: Huge_Position890
replies.body: You were right, and thank you. The archive is time-sorted with hundreds of signals per bar, so each 200-signal block was roughly one bar. I re-ran it as a moving-block bootstrap over time windows with all coins kept together, a rule I wrote down before running. The gaps don't move (+0.39 BUY, +0.30 SELL), but the uncertainty is 2–2.5x larger: with 7-day windows gap/SE is 1.4 and 1.3, and both 95% intervals include zero. So the filter's value isn't shown. I've added a correction at the top of the post. The pooling arithmetic still holds; the significance doesn't.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: That’s the right check, and the effective sample being closer to days than signals is the main concern. Resampling whole windows with all coins together would likely widen the interval while leaving the average gap unchanged.

replies.author: Huge_Position890
replies.body:
Exactly what happened. I ran it with 7-day windows, all coins kept together: the gaps didn't move (+0.39 / +0.30), the intervals widened 2–2.5x, and both now include zero. I've added a correction to the top of the post.

Your effective-sample point is the real lesson. The 99k signals sound like a lot, but they cover only \~50 days of 4H bars, so with weekly windows it's roughly seven independent weeks. I'll re-run in late November on about twice the data, with time-window resampling from the start.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Thanks for running it and for adding the correction to the top of the post. Seven independent weeks is the honest sample size, and keeping the effect size while the interval widens is the useful part: it says the effect is plausible but not yet established. Thanks for the open update.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Measuring each direction separately and showing the Simpson’s paradox with the 70% versus 41% BUY mix is the useful part, and the pre-registered 30% estimate adds credibility. I’d add one thing to the null: the 24h forward returns overlap and coins move together, so resampling whole calendar windows with all coins kept together (a block bootstrap by time, not by signal count) would show whether the SNR of 3 to 4 survives, since the effective sample is probably closer to the number of independent days than to 99,409. A per-month split of the kept-minus-removed difference would also show whether one rally carries it. Funding Rate Radar at Cymetica shows perp funding across venues, which is one input for the regime label

replies.author: Huge_Position890
replies.body:
Thanks. I ran the time-window bootstrap after the first comment (7-day windows, all coins together): same gaps, intervals 2–2.5x wider, both include zero. The correction is at the top of the post.

The per-month split was a good call, and it confirms it. August carries most of it: about 60% of the signals, and the only month that's clearly positive in both directions (+0.40 BUY, +0.43 SELL). July and September flip sign in at least one direction. So it's one period's effect, not a stable one. I'll re-test in late November on roughly twice the data, by time window from the start.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Thanks for running the per-month split and reporting it plainly. If August holds most of the signals and flips sign in July and September, then it's one period's effect, and saying so in the post is the honest read. Thanks for the open update.
